mcqs.explanation: Multiprocessing can provide hardware-level parallel execution.

mcqs.topic: 1.2.1 Desktop OS categories and processing models
mcqs.question: Can one core support multitasking?
options: No, multitasking always requires two sockets
Yes, by switching execution among tasks
No, every task needs a dedicated machine
Yes, because instructions never take time
mcqs.explanation: Time-sliced execution can make several tasks progress on one core.

mcqs.topic: 1.2.1 Desktop OS categories and processing models
mcqs.question: What makes a real-time response successful?
options: Having the highest advertised clock speed
Meeting the required deadline as well as producing the right result
mcqs.explanation: Timing requirements are part of correctness in real-time work.

mcqs.topic: 1.2.1 Desktop OS categories and processing models
mcqs.question: Which example most clearly uses a network OS service?
options: A standalone calculator changes its display colour
A disconnected notebook changes a wallpaper
An editor checks a spelling mistake
A central server authenticates users and shares a print queue
mcqs.explanation: Central network accounts and shared services are network-oriented functions.

mcqs.topic: 1.2.1 Desktop OS categories and processing models
mcqs.question: Are multitasking and multiprocessing mutually exclusive?
options: No, one system can support both
Yes, neither can use an OS
Yes, they describe the same single feature only
No, because both mean batch printing
mcqs.explanation: One describes task progress; the other describes processing resources.

mcqs.topic: 1.2.1 Desktop OS categories and processing models
mcqs.question: Which situation best illustrates time sharing?
options: A document is printed only once a year
A disk stores every byte at the same address
Interactive users receive scheduled portions of CPU time
A monitor splits its plastic casing
mcqs.explanation: Scheduling time among interactive tasks supports responsive shared use.

mcqs.question: Which is an example of a mobile operating system?
mcqs.explanation: Android manages mobile applications and device resources.

mcqs.question: What can differ between Android devices?
options: Whether all devices have identical hardware
Whether every app is automatically trustworthy
mcqs.explanation: Device makers and support policies affect update availability.

mcqs.question: What is the current name for Apple iPad system software?
mcqs.explanation: iPadOS is distinct from the iPhone name iOS.

mcqs.question: Does updating one app necessarily upgrade the OS?
options: Yes, every app replaces the kernel
Yes, a font download changes the OS version
No, application and OS updates are different operations
No, because apps can never be updated
mcqs.explanation: An application release and a system release have different scopes.

mcqs.question: Which permission practice is appropriate for a mobile app?
options: Share a device passcode with every app author
Grant only the access needed for its task
mcqs.explanation: Least privilege limits unnecessary access.

mcqs.question: Why should a student record the actual lab OS version?
options: Versions and support status change over time
Every mobile device has one permanent version
An OS version proves every app is safe
mcqs.explanation: Recording the observed version avoids unsupported current-version claims.

mcqs.question: Which comparison is correct?
options: A desktop OS and a mobile OS both manage resources, with different usage priorities
mcqs.explanation: Resource management is shared, while interfaces and constraints differ.

mcqs.question: Which is the best explanation of an OS limitation?
options: It cannot guarantee that every application or hardware component is fault-free
It makes every computer infinitely fast
It prevents all possible user mistakes
It removes the need for maintenance
mcqs.explanation: Resource management does not prove universal reliability.

mcqs.question: What is a system call?
options: A telephone number printed in a file
A controlled request for an OS service
A guarantee that a program has no bugs
mcqs.explanation: System calls provide a defined entry to operating-system services.

mcqs.question: Which description is a command-line interface?
mcqs.explanation: A command-line interface lets users express requests as commands.

mcqs.question: Which distinction is correct?
options: A GUI is always the entire kernel
A graphical interface and a command shell can request the same OS services
A system call is a display resolution
mcqs.explanation: Interfaces present requests; underlying services manage operations.

mcqs.question: Why use protection boundaries?
options: To prevent unrestricted access to other processes and protected resources
To stop every application from saving
mcqs.explanation: Boundaries support isolation and controlled sharing.

mcqs.question: What does memory management maintain?
options: Only the names of print jobs
Controlled address spaces and memory allocations
mcqs.explanation: The OS allocates and protects memory used by execution contexts.

mcqs.question: Does virtual memory create new physical RAM?
options: Yes, every disk byte becomes a RAM chip
Yes, it removes every page fault
No, it provides an address-space and mapping mechanism
No, because programs never use addresses
mcqs.explanation: Virtual memory manages mappings; it does not manufacture physical memory.

mcqs.question: Which task belongs to process management?
options: Changing the wording of a paragraph
Scheduling a ready process for CPU time
mcqs.explanation: The OS scheduler allocates processing opportunities.

mcqs.question: What is saved during a context switch?
options: Execution state needed to resume the previous context
mcqs.explanation: Registers and other context information allow execution to resume.

mcqs.question: Which operation is file management?
mcqs.explanation: File management handles named persistent objects and their operations.

mcqs.question: What is authentication?
options: Establishing the identity of a user or service
mcqs.explanation: Authentication concerns identity; authorisation concerns allowed actions.

mcqs.question: What is authorisation?
options: Deciding whether an identity may perform an action
Showing that every file is public
mcqs.explanation: Permissions determine which operations an authenticated identity can perform.

mcqs.question: Does changing a file extension reliably convert its contents?
options: Yes, all formats have identical contents
Yes, renaming a file edits every byte
No, because files cannot be renamed
No, conversion requires an appropriate application or format operation
mcqs.explanation: Names and data representation are different properties.

mcqs.question: Which example describes a circular wait?
options: A program finishes and releases its file
A waits for a resource held by B while B waits for one held by A
A user closes an unused window
A process prints one result and exits
mcqs.explanation: The dependency cycle can prevent all participants from making progress.

mcqs.question: Which strategy can prevent a circular resource-acquisition pattern?
options: Acquire every lock in a random order
Assume that a faster CPU removes all locks
Acquire resources in a consistent global order
mcqs.explanation: A consistent ordering prevents cycles in that acquisition pattern.

mcqs.question: Is every slow process deadlocked?
options: Yes, any delay is circular wait
Yes, a slow display proves a deadlock
No, it may be computing, waiting for I/O or waiting for scheduling
mcqs.explanation: Deadlock requires a particular blocking dependency, not simply elapsed time.

mcqs.question: What can a critical section protect?
options: The colour of the computer case
A shared update that must not interleave unsafely
The physical length of a cable
The name of an unrelated folder
mcqs.explanation: Coordinated access can prevent inconsistent shared-state updates.

mcqs.question: Which condition belongs to the standard resource-deadlock model?
mcqs.explanation: A participant can hold one resource while waiting for another.

mcqs.question: What is a race condition?
options: A result depends on an unsafe timing or interleaving of operations
A program always executes in one fixed order
A file is compressed with a password
A printer runs out of paper
mcqs.explanation: Unsynchronised access can make results depend on timing.

mcqs.question: What does least privilege mean?
options: Give the access required for the task, rather than unrestricted access
mcqs.explanation: Limited permissions reduce unnecessary exposure while allowing the required work.

mcqs.question: Which statement about OS security is sound?
options: Installing an OS proves that every action is safe
All administrators should share one password
It supports controls, but applications and users must use them correctly
Auditing removes the need for access controls
mcqs.explanation: An OS supplies mechanisms, not a guarantee that every policy or application is correct.

mcqs.question: What is a process?
options: Only an executable file sitting unused on disk
A running program instance with managed execution state and resources
mcqs.explanation: A process includes active execution context, not only stored instructions.

mcqs.question: Can the same executable have two process instances?
options: Yes, separate instances can have different state and resources
No, an executable can run only once in its lifetime
No, all programs share one process identifier forever
Yes, but neither can have memory
mcqs.explanation: Separate process instances can execute the same program.

mcqs.question: What does a PID identify?
options: A permanent identity for a person
A process in the OS process-management context
mcqs.explanation: Process identifiers are managed by the OS and can be reused after a process ends.

mcqs.question: Which statement distinguishes program and process?
options: A program is stored instructions; a process is an executing instance
A process is always a text document
A program always has a running thread even when unused
The terms always refer only to physical RAM chips
mcqs.explanation: Execution state distinguishes a process from the program file.

mcqs.question: Which state means eligible for execution but not currently scheduled?
options: Waiting for an unfinished I/O event
mcqs.explanation: A ready task is eligible and awaits CPU allocation.

mcqs.question: A running task requests a blocking file read. Which transition fits the model?
mcqs.explanation: The task blocks until the required operation completes.

mcqs.question: After a blocked task receives its I/O completion, which state normally follows in this model?
mcqs.explanation: The event removes the block; scheduling is still needed.

mcqs.question: What causes ready to running?
options: An unrelated user changing a wallpaper
mcqs.explanation: Dispatch selects an eligible execution context.

mcqs.question: Which transition can a timer-related pre-emption cause?
options: Terminated to new with the same execution context
New directly to blocked after completion
mcqs.explanation: A still-runnable task can be returned to the ready set.

mcqs.question: Do all real OSs report exactly the same five state names?
options: No, the five-state model is a simplified teaching model
Yes, all internal implementations are identical
Yes, a sixth state is physically impossible
No, because no OS tracks states
mcqs.explanation: Real systems may add states or use different names and representations.

mcqs.question: Which state describes completed execution?
mcqs.explanation: Termination marks the end of the process execution.

mcqs.question: An editor waits for input. Does low CPU use prove a deadlock?
options: No, waiting for a normal event can be expected
Yes, every idle application is deadlocked
Yes, every keyboard wait is circular wait
No, because editors never have processes
mcqs.explanation: Expected blocking must be distinguished from a deadlock dependency.

mcqs.topic: 3.3 PCB, process operations and context switching
mcqs.question: Which information commonly belongs in a PCB?
options: The colour of every desktop icon
Process state and saved execution context
The physical width of the monitor
mcqs.explanation: A PCB tracks process-management state and resource references.

mcqs.topic: 3.3 PCB, process operations and context switching
mcqs.question: What does the program counter represent conceptually?
options: The number of installed applications only
The instruction location used to continue execution
A permanent count of all files
The number of users on the Internet
mcqs.explanation: An instruction pointer helps identify where execution proceeds.

mcqs.topic: 3.3 PCB, process operations and context switching
mcqs.question: Is context switching free of overhead?
options: Yes, it always takes zero time
Yes, it performs every user calculation at once
No, because it replaces the CPU physically
No, saving and restoring state uses resources
mcqs.explanation: Context-switch work consumes processing time.

mcqs.topic: 3.3 PCB, process operations and context switching
mcqs.question: How is suspension different from termination?
options: Both always erase the program file
Suspension pauses progress while termination ends execution
Suspension always creates a new operating system
Termination guarantees all unsaved work is recovered
mcqs.explanation: A paused execution context can potentially resume; an ended execution does not continue as the same active process.

mcqs.question: What is a thread?
options: A type of copper network connector
A file extension for a spreadsheet
An execution flow within a process
mcqs.explanation: Threads provide execution contexts within a process.

mcqs.question: Which resource is normally shared by threads of one process?
options: One compulsory identical stack for every thread
Every register value at every instant
mcqs.explanation: Threads share address-space resources but maintain their own execution context.

mcqs.question: Which item is normally private to each thread?
options: Its execution stack and register context
The process-wide address space as a whole
Every file on the entire machine
mcqs.explanation: Each thread needs its own state for call frames and execution.

mcqs.question: Why must shared-thread updates be coordinated?
options: A thread always executes every operation atomically
Coordination is needed only for monitor brightness
Unsafe interleavings can cause races or inconsistent results
mcqs.explanation: Shared mutable data can be affected by execution timing.

mcqs.question: What should an installation plan identify first?
options: The authorised target device, edition, requirements and recovery plan
mcqs.explanation: Installation choices must match the authorised hardware and data-recovery requirements.

mcqs.question: Is the syllabus hardware baseline a guarantee for every workload?
options: Yes, all software has identical demands
Yes, disk capacity determines every driver
No, compatibility and workload requirements still need checking
mcqs.explanation: A course baseline does not replace edition-specific and workload-specific checks.

mcqs.question: Where should a learner practise partition-changing installation work?
options: The only copy of a family photo disk
An assigned disposable lab disk or VM
mcqs.explanation: Partition operations belong in an authorised lab with recoverable data.

mcqs.topic: 4.2 Bootable USB, optical media and Rufus
mcqs.question: Does copying an ISO as a normal USB file always make bootable installation media?
options: No, an appropriate media-preparation operation is needed
Yes, the file name alone changes firmware
Yes, every USB is automatically bootable
No, because USB drives cannot hold files
mcqs.explanation: Bootable media requires a suitable layout and boot files.

mcqs.topic: 4.2 Bootable USB, optical media and Rufus
mcqs.question: What must be checked immediately before writing an installation USB?
options: Only the colour of the USB casing
Whether every other disk can also be erased
The exact target device and whether its data may be erased
mcqs.explanation: Writing installation media can replace the selected device contents.

mcqs.topic: 4.2 Bootable USB, optical media and Rufus
mcqs.question: What should boot-mode and partition settings match?
options: The assigned firmware and installation design
mcqs.explanation: UEFI/legacy and partition choices must fit the lab target.

mcqs.question: Which checkpoint is essential before disk-changing setup actions?
options: Choose the first listed disk automatically
Confirm the intended target against the lab inventory
mcqs.explanation: The selected disk must be the authorised lab target.

mcqs.question: What should follow the first successful sign-in?
options: Assume all hardware is correct forever
Verify devices, edition, network, updates and recovery requirements
Share the account password with the whole class
mcqs.explanation: Post-installation verification checks actual system operation.

mcqs.question: What should a missing expected disk prompt?
options: Investigation of the lab configuration or driver requirement
A claim that installation is complete
mcqs.explanation: Unexpected storage information must be resolved before proceeding.

mcqs.question: What is a partition?
options: The name of an email recipient
A defined region of a disk address space
mcqs.explanation: Partitions describe storage regions, not application document names.

mcqs.question: Does quick formatting prove secure destruction of all old data?
options: Yes, every byte is always overwritten many times
Yes, it physically destroys the disk
No, because formatting never affects a file system
mcqs.explanation: Formatting and validated data sanitisation are different operations.

mcqs.question: Why distinguish a disk from a drive letter?
options: Every disk must always be C:
A letter is the physical serial number
A drive letter proves an OS licence
A disk can contain multiple volumes, and letters are logical access names
mcqs.explanation: Logical names do not uniquely describe physical storage.

mcqs.question: What does a shortcut normally contain?
options: A reference to a target item
A guaranteed independent backup of every target byte
mcqs.explanation: A shortcut provides access to a target; it does not necessarily copy the target data.

mcqs.question: What is the taskbar used for?
mcqs.explanation: The taskbar is part of the graphical interaction environment.

mcqs.question: How does locking differ from signing out?
options: They always have exactly the same effect on applications
Locking protects access to the existing session; signing out ends the user session
mcqs.explanation: Session termination and screen locking have different purposes.

mcqs.question: What should a hardware driver match?
options: Only the colour of the hardware
Any software with a similar file name
The actual device and supported OS/architecture
mcqs.explanation: Driver compatibility is specific to the device and operating environment.

mcqs.question: Which tool helps inspect Windows device identity and problems?
mcqs.explanation: Device Manager presents installed device information and status.

mcqs.question: How should an approved application normally be removed?
options: Delete random files from the system folder
mcqs.explanation: Supported uninstall procedures handle application components and registrations.

mcqs.question: Which check is useful after a NIC driver installation?
options: Assume a completion dialog proves connectivity
Verify adapter status and the intended network connection
mcqs.explanation: Functional verification checks the device's intended operation.

mcqs.question: Which account type suits routine student work?
options: A standard user with necessary permissions
A shared unrestricted administrator for every task
An account with a publicly posted password
mcqs.explanation: Routine work should use the privileges needed for its tasks.

mcqs.question: What should be used for a forgotten personal account password?
options: An attempt to bypass someone else's account
The official owner recovery route or authorised reset procedure
Deleting every account without a backup
mcqs.explanation: Recovery must follow the owner's authorised process.

mcqs.question: Does resetting a password necessarily reveal the previous password?
options: Yes, the old password is always displayed
Yes, every reset recovers all encrypted files automatically
No, because accounts cannot be reset
mcqs.explanation: A reset changes authentication information; it does not necessarily disclose the old secret.

mcqs.question: Does tablet mode add touch hardware to a non-touch display?
options: Yes, software grows a new sensor
Yes, every monitor becomes a tablet
No, because touch devices cannot use Windows
mcqs.explanation: Interface settings do not manufacture touch-sensitive hardware.

mcqs.question: What is a Windows virtual desktop?
options: A completely separate virtual machine automatically
An organised workspace for windows within the signed-in environment
mcqs.explanation: Virtual desktops organise application windows; they are not independent installed systems.

mcqs.question: Does matching the workgroup name alone guarantee file sharing?
options: Yes, it assigns every host an address
No, connectivity, identity, permissions and service settings also matter
No, because Windows cannot share files
mcqs.explanation: Workgroup naming is only one part of the environment.

mcqs.question: What does a Wi-Fi connection prove by itself?
options: A local wireless association, not necessarily working Internet access
That the ISP account is paid
mcqs.explanation: Wireless association and end-to-end Internet service are separate checks.

mcqs.question: Where should a DSL lab obtain ISP-specific settings?
options: From a random guess applied to a live router
mcqs.explanation: DSL service parameters are specific to the provider and authorised connection.

mcqs.topic: 4.16-4.18 Input settings, Urdu, printing and scanning
mcqs.question: Which combination is useful for Urdu document entry?
options: An Urdu input layout, Unicode-capable font and appropriate paragraph direction
Only increasing the monitor refresh rate
mcqs.explanation: Input, glyph support and text direction serve different parts of the task.

mcqs.topic: 4.16-4.18 Input settings, Urdu, printing and scanning
mcqs.question: What should follow printer installation?
options: Print and inspect a test page from the intended queue
Assume every queue points to the same device
mcqs.explanation: A test page checks the actual print path.

mcqs.topic: 4.16-4.18 Input settings, Urdu, printing and scanning
mcqs.question: What should follow a scan?
options: Reopen the saved output and check readability, orientation and destination
Assume every preview was saved automatically
Choose the largest possible file for every task
Delete the original before checking the output
mcqs.explanation: Verification checks the saved result, not only the scanning dialog.

mcqs.topic: 5.1 Workgroups and an authorised lab network
mcqs.question: What distinguishes a workgroup from an AD domain?
options: A workgroup automatically makes every host a domain controller
A workgroup normally uses peer/local account organisation rather than central domain membership
A workgroup is the same as an IP subnet mask
A domain can never have central accounts
mcqs.explanation: Workgroup naming and domain-based directory administration are different concepts.

mcqs.topic: 5.1 Workgroups and an authorised lab network
mcqs.question: What does a successful ping establish most directly?
options: Permission to read every shared folder
An ICMP reachability result for that particular test
Proof that a printer is installed
Proof that all DNS names resolve
mcqs.explanation: Application services and permissions need separate checks.

mcqs.topic: 5.1 Workgroups and an authorised lab network
mcqs.question: What is the first step in a safe sharing exercise?
options: Use an authorised isolated lab and an addressing/access plan
Share a personal home directory publicly
mcqs.explanation: The network and data must be appropriate to the lab task.

mcqs.question: What determines whether a destination is in the local IPv4 subnet?
options: The address together with the subnet prefix/mask
mcqs.explanation: The prefix identifies the network portion used for the on-link decision.

mcqs.question: Which is an ordinary host address in 192.168.50.0/24?
mcqs.explanation: The .0 network and .255 broadcast addresses are not ordinary hosts in this /24.

mcqs.question: What is a default gateway used for?
options: Forwarding traffic toward destinations outside the local subnet when the route requires it
mcqs.explanation: The gateway must be a reachable router that provides the intended forwarding path.

mcqs.question: Why avoid duplicate static host addresses?
options: They can create address conflicts and unreliable communication
They replace the need for a subnet mask
mcqs.explanation: Each ordinary active host interface needs an appropriate non-conflicting address in the lab.

mcqs.question: Which command shows detailed Windows adapter configuration?
mcqs.explanation: ipconfig /all reports detailed adapter configuration.

mcqs.question: Why should a shared folder be tested as the learner?
options: All accounts always have identical permissions
A shared folder has no access rules
A folder name authenticates every user
Administrator access does not prove that the learner has the intended permissions
mcqs.explanation: Effective access must be tested with the actual intended identity.

mcqs.question: What can affect access to a Windows shared file?
options: Both share and file-system permissions, identity and service settings
Only the number of folder letters
mcqs.explanation: Network access depends on several coordinated controls.

mcqs.question: If a share works by address but not by name, what should be investigated?
mcqs.explanation: A naming failure can remain even when the underlying network path works.

mcqs.question: What should a training share contain?
options: The only copy of private client documents
A public list of real passwords
mcqs.explanation: Use data and permissions appropriate to the authorised exercise.

mcqs.question: What should be verified before sharing a printer?
options: The host can use the correct installed printer successfully
The queue icon has a favourite colour
mcqs.explanation: The underlying host/device print path must work first.

mcqs.question: What is a useful client-side sharing test?
options: Assume the host test proves every client works
Print a labelled page and inspect it at the intended device
mcqs.explanation: The test verifies client permissions, queue selection and actual output.

mcqs.question: Does sharing a queue automatically provide compatible drivers to every client?
options: Yes, every driver works on every platform
Yes, a queue name changes CPU architecture
No, because printers never use drivers
No, client compatibility and configuration still need checking
mcqs.explanation: Shared access does not eliminate platform and driver requirements.

mcqs.question: Which evidence best confirms a shared-file copy?
options: Only state that a progress bar appeared
Open the copied sample and compare its expected contents
Only count the characters in the share name
mcqs.explanation: Verification must inspect the actual transferred result.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of an acceptance table?
options: Define identities, permitted operations and expected results before testing
mcqs.explanation: Expected results make the demonstration assessable.

mcqs.question: Which response to an access-denied error is appropriate?
options: Assume the cable must be physically broken
Check the identity and effective permissions for the requested operation
mcqs.explanation: An authorisation symptom should prompt relevant access checks.

mcqs.question: What should follow a temporary lab sharing exercise?
options: Restore the approved baseline and remove unneeded training access
Leave every training account publicly privileged
Publish all credentials with the report
mcqs.explanation: Lab cleanup should follow the authorised configuration plan.

mcqs.question: Why change one justified setting at a time?
options: It guarantees the first guess is right
It helps associate the observed result with a particular change
It replaces the need for an original symptom
mcqs.explanation: Controlled troubleshooting produces clearer evidence.

mcqs.topic: 6.1-6.2 Server purpose, clients and a controlled installation
mcqs.question: What defines a server in a client-server interaction?
options: It must have the largest monitor
It cannot also use another service
It provides a requested service to clients
mcqs.explanation: Client and server describe service relationships.

mcqs.topic: 6.1-6.2 Server purpose, clients and a controlled installation
mcqs.question: What is a Windows Server role?
options: Only the colour of a desktop theme
A guarantee that every service should be enabled
A set of components for a defined service function
The number of physical keys on a keyboard
mcqs.explanation: Roles organise services such as directory, DNS, DHCP and printing.

mcqs.topic: 6.1-6.2 Server purpose, clients and a controlled installation
mcqs.question: Where should a training server with DHCP or directory roles run?
mcqs.explanation: Lab services must not interfere with real clients.

mcqs.topic: 6.1-6.2 Server purpose, clients and a controlled installation
mcqs.question: What should guide selection of installed roles?
options: Install every role regardless of need
mcqs.explanation: A service design determines the necessary roles and configuration.

mcqs.question: What is a practical purpose of central print services?
options: Turn every document into a domain account
Remove the need for printer readiness
Manage shared printer queues and authorised client use
mcqs.explanation: Central administration manages queues, devices and access.

mcqs.question: Which output verifies an authorised client print path?
options: A labelled page produced by the intended physical printer
mcqs.explanation: The actual result verifies the end-to-end task.

mcqs.question: What does AD DS organise?
options: Directory objects such as users, groups and computers
mcqs.explanation: AD DS stores and makes directory information available through controlled services.

mcqs.question: What is a domain controller?
options: Any cable attached to a switch
A server hosting the domain directory service
A renamed workgroup on every desktop
mcqs.explanation: A domain controller has a directory-service role.

mcqs.question: Why does a domain lab need working DNS?
options: Clients must locate the domain and its services through appropriate name records
DNS is the same as a print queue
mcqs.explanation: Correct name resolution is important to directory-service discovery.

mcqs.question: Does joining a domain prove that all application permissions are correct?
options: Yes, it grants every user unrestricted access
No, because domains have no users
No, the intended operations and policies still need testing
mcqs.explanation: Membership and specific effective access are separate matters.

mcqs.question: What is the main purpose of DHCP?
options: Resolve every domain name by itself
Convert every switch into a router
mcqs.explanation: DHCP automates address and option configuration.

mcqs.question: What does a DHCP exclusion do?
options: Publishes those addresses as public passwords
Keeps selected addresses out of general pool assignment
Converts an address into a domain name
mcqs.explanation: Exclusions protect addresses intended for other controlled use.

mcqs.question: Which sequence describes a common initial DHCP exchange?
mcqs.explanation: The DORA sequence is the common introductory acquisition model.

mcqs.question: What should be checked after a DHCP lab client connects?
options: Its actual lease, address, prefix, gateway and DNS options
mcqs.explanation: The received configuration must match the intended scope and options.

mcqs.question: Which DNS record maps a name to an IPv4 address?
mcqs.explanation: A records contain IPv4 address information.

mcqs.question: Which DNS record contains an IPv6 address?
mcqs.explanation: AAAA records contain IPv6 address information.

mcqs.question: Does successful DNS resolution prove that an application service is reachable?
options: Yes, a name record guarantees every TCP port
No, routing, policy and the service can still fail
No, because names cannot map to addresses
mcqs.explanation: Name resolution and application reachability are separate checks.

mcqs.question: What can affect whether a repeated query reaches a server again immediately?
options: Only the file extension of an essay
mcqs.explanation: A resolver can use a cached result within its applicable lifetime.

mcqs.question: What is WINS primarily associated with?
mcqs.explanation: WINS addresses a legacy naming context.

mcqs.question: Which comparison is correct?
options: DHCP supplies configuration while DNS answers DNS name-record queries
DHCP and DNS are identical operations
AD DS is only a printer driver
mcqs.explanation: The services have distinct responsibilities.

mcqs.question: Should WINS be installed on every new network just because it appears in the syllabus?
options: Yes, it is required for every modern DNS lookup
Yes, it replaces all access controls
No, because historical concepts cannot be studied
No, assess an actual legacy requirement
mcqs.explanation: Learning a legacy function does not justify an unnecessary production role.

mcqs.question: Which test matches a DNS role?
options: Query a known training name and compare the expected record
Only rename the case of a folder
mcqs.explanation: A DNS test should inspect a name-resolution result.

mcqs.question: What is a program?
options: Instructions expressing a task for a computer
mcqs.explanation: Programs specify operations; hardware supplies the means to execute them.

mcqs.question: Which description fits assembly language?
options: A universal language requiring no translation
Symbolic instructions closely related to an instruction set
mcqs.explanation: An assembler translates the symbolic representation for the relevant target.

mcqs.question: Which is a high-level language?
mcqs.explanation: Python expresses general computations at a high level.

mcqs.question: Why define valid input before writing code?
options: Correct behaviour depends on the intended problem and accepted data
Running code automatically proves the requirement
Every possible input must have the same result

mcqs.explanation: Both default and supplied-argument paths need checking.

mcqs.topic: 8.4 Default arguments and variable argument lists
mcqs.question: Which factorial function result is correct for n=5?
mcqs.explanation: 5 factorial is 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

mcqs.question: What does forward(100) change?
mcqs.explanation: Forward movement changes the turtle position.

mcqs.question: Does left(90) alone draw a line?
options: No, it changes heading without moving
Yes, it always draws a square
No, because angles cannot be changed
mcqs.explanation: Rotation and translation are different operations.

mcqs.question: What does penup control?
options: Whether Excel files can be read
mcqs.explanation: Pen state controls drawing during movement.

mcqs.question: Which environment is required by the ordinary desktop Turtle examples?
options: Any browser compiler without checking support
Desktop Python with working Tk/GUI support
mcqs.explanation: A GUI dependency cannot be assumed in every browser runtime.

mcqs.question: What can a headless geometry trace verify?
options: That every desktop display driver works
That a GUI window definitely appeared
That all event-loop behaviour was exercised
mcqs.explanation: Logic-level tracing is different from actual GUI verification.

mcqs.question: What does back(distance) do?
options: Always turn left by that many degrees
mcqs.explanation: Back movement uses the current orientation but the opposite travel direction.

mcqs.topic: 9.3 Lines, squares, rectangles, circles and stars
mcqs.question: What turn angle is used between sides of the square example?
mcqs.explanation: Four equal sides with right-angle turns form the square path.

mcqs.topic: 9.3 Lines, squares, rectangles, circles and stars
mcqs.question: Which lengths form the rectangle example?
mcqs.explanation: Opposite rectangle sides have equal lengths.

mcqs.topic: 9.3 Lines, squares, rectangles, circles and stars
mcqs.question: What turn draws the five-point star path shown here?
mcqs.explanation: The pentagram uses a 144-degree turn after each equal side.

mcqs.topic: 9.3 Lines, squares, rectangles, circles and stars
mcqs.question: What is the total turn over five 144-degree turns?
mcqs.explanation: 5 × 144 equals 720.

mcqs.topic: 9.3 Lines, squares, rectangles, circles and stars
mcqs.question: Which Turtle operation directly supports drawing a circle?
mcqs.explanation: circle is a Turtle drawing operation.

mcqs.topic: 9.3 Lines, squares, rectangles, circles and stars
mcqs.question: Why lift the pen before relocating between separate lines?
options: To change every turn into a list
To replace the coordinate system with Excel
To avoid drawing an unwanted connector
mcqs.explanation: Movement with pen up does not draw the connecting segment.

mcqs.topic: 9.4 Reading and writing Excel with pandas
mcqs.question: What is the correct library name for the syllabus Excel task?
options: panda as the documented package name here
mcqs.explanation: The table/file-I/O library is named pandas.

mcqs.topic: 9.4 Reading and writing Excel with pandas
mcqs.question: What does pandas.read_excel do?
options: Guarantee preservation of every Excel macro
Read worksheet data into a tabular object
mcqs.explanation: The operation reads spreadsheet data through an appropriate engine.

mcqs.topic: 9.4 Reading and writing Excel with pandas
mcqs.question: Which operation writes a DataFrame to an Excel file?
mcqs.explanation: to_excel supports writing spreadsheet data.

mcqs.topic: 9.4 Reading and writing Excel with pandas
mcqs.question: Why use index=False in the supplied table-writing lab?
options: To remove all column headers automatically
To avoid an extra output column for the DataFrame index
mcqs.explanation: The intended worksheet table does not include the index as a data column.

mcqs.topic: 9.4 Reading and writing Excel with pandas
mcqs.question: What should follow writing a practice workbook?
options: Assume the save call proves every requirement
Read it back and compare expected rows, columns and values
mcqs.explanation: Round-trip checks validate the actual saved table.

mcqs.topic: 9.4 Reading and writing Excel with pandas
mcqs.question: Why specify sheet_name when reading a particular sheet?
options: A workbook can contain more than one sheet
Every workbook must contain only one cell
mcqs.explanation: The requested worksheet should be identified explicitly.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: Which tool provides array-oriented numerical computing?
mcqs.explanation: NumPy supplies numerical array operations.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: Which tool is commonly used for plotting data?
mcqs.explanation: Matplotlib is used for data visualisation/plotting.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: Which named item is a separate programming language?
mcqs.explanation: Kotlin is not a Python library.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: What is Django?
mcqs.explanation: Django supports web application development.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: What is MicroPython oriented toward?
mcqs.explanation: MicroPython adapts Python execution to constrained-device contexts.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: What does Tkinter require for a normal interactive window?
options: A working Tk/GUI environment and event handling
mcqs.explanation: GUI creation and interaction need the relevant desktop facilities.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: What does NumPy elementwise multiplication do in the example?
mcqs.explanation: Each value is multiplied by the corresponding value.

mcqs.topic: 9.5 Other tools and the Kotlin classification correction
mcqs.question: Does importing Pygame alone create a complete working game?
options: Yes, it invents all game rules automatically
Only if the module name is uppercase
Yes, no event handling is needed
mcqs.explanation: A game still needs application logic, events, rendering and timing.

mcqs.topic: 8.1-8.2 Modem, DSL and the authorised lab boundary
mcqs.question: Which role forwards packets between IP networks?
mcqs.explanation: Routing connects different IP networks.

mcqs.topic: 8.1-8.2 Modem, DSL and the authorised lab boundary
mcqs.question: Can a consumer device combine modem, router and access-point functions?
options: No, every device can have exactly one role
Only if it has no power
Only when used as a printer
mcqs.explanation: Several network functions can be integrated in one product.

mcqs.topic: 8.1-8.2 Modem, DSL and the authorised lab boundary
mcqs.question: Where should ISP-specific DSL parameters come from?
options: A guessed public example applied to a live connection
mcqs.explanation: Connection parameters must match the authorised service.

mcqs.topic: 8.1-8.2 Modem, DSL and the authorised lab boundary
mcqs.question: Why avoid a casual factory reset of a working subscriber router?
options: It can erase required connection and access settings
It always improves every connection automatically
mcqs.explanation: Resetting is a configuration-changing action requiring a recovery plan.

mcqs.topic: 8.1-8.2 Modem, DSL and the authorised lab boundary
mcqs.question: Does a Wi-Fi indicator prove DSL synchronisation and Internet service?
options: Yes, every status layer is identical
Yes, no other test is needed
Only if the SSID is short
mcqs.explanation: Wireless association, DSL link and end-to-end service are distinct checks.

mcqs.topic: 8.1-8.2 Modem, DSL and the authorised lab boundary
mcqs.question: Which equipment belongs in this configuration exercise?
options: An authorised spare device or isolated simulation
mcqs.explanation: The exercise must remain within the assigned training environment.

mcqs.question: Which termination pair is straight-through?
options: T568A at one end and T568B at the other as the standard straight-through definition
Random conductor order at each end
mcqs.explanation: A straight-through lead uses corresponding pin assignments at both ends.

mcqs.question: What are T568B pins 1 and 2?
mcqs.explanation: These are the first pair assignments in the listed T568B scheme.

mcqs.question: Why use a cable tester after crimping?
options: Prove every possible Ethernet performance requirement with any basic tester
Assign an IP address to the cable
Check the actual conductor wire map and continuity
mcqs.explanation: A basic tester checks defined wiring properties, not all performance characteristics.

mcqs.question: Does an auto-MDI-X link prove that a lead has the intended training pin map?
options: Yes, the port rewires the actual connector permanently
No, because auto-MDI-X always prevents links
mcqs.explanation: Port adaptation and physical wire-map verification are different matters.

mcqs.topic: 8.4 Legacy crossover cables and direct connections
mcqs.question: Which termination pair is the listed legacy 10/100 crossover example?
mcqs.explanation: The schemes exchange the listed transmit/receive pair positions.

mcqs.topic: 8.4 Legacy crossover cables and direct connections
mcqs.question: Which pair positions cross in the described legacy 10/100 example?
mcqs.explanation: The exercise concerns the historical 10/100 transmit/receive pair mapping.

mcqs.topic: 8.4 Legacy crossover cables and direct connections
mcqs.question: Do two hosts in one /24 always need a gateway to communicate directly?
options: Yes, a gateway is required for every local frame
No, ordinary same-subnet traffic is on-link
Yes, DNS is always the gateway
mcqs.explanation: A gateway is used when the routing decision requires an off-link path.

mcqs.topic: 8.4 Legacy crossover cables and direct connections
mcqs.question: Why mention auto-MDI-X?
options: It removes every need for address configuration
Modern interface adaptation can change the observed cable requirement
It is a type of printed homework
mcqs.explanation: Do not generalise legacy cabling rules to every modern interface.

mcqs.question: Which command reports the local Windows host name?
mcqs.explanation: hostname reports the local computer name.

mcqs.question: Which command shows detailed adapter configuration?
mcqs.explanation: The /all option adds adapter configuration details.

mcqs.question: What does arp -a primarily display?
options: A guaranteed complete directory of every Internet device
mcqs.explanation: The cache contains learned address-resolution information.

mcqs.question: What does a ping success establish?
options: An ICMP result for the tested destination/path
mcqs.explanation: ICMP reachability is not a universal service or authorisation test.

mcqs.question: Do tracert asterisks necessarily prove the whole route is unusable?
options: Yes, every asterisk means the disk failed
Yes, all following hops must be physically missing
No, because tracert never sends packets
No, responses can be filtered or absent
mcqs.explanation: Hop-response behaviour must be interpreted with other evidence.

mcqs.question: When are release/renew appropriate in this workbook?
options: On every live adapter regardless of impact
On the assigned DHCP lab adapter when requested
As a way to correct every static address automatically
As a replacement for recording symptoms
mcqs.explanation: The operations affect DHCP configuration and can disrupt a connection.

mcqs.question: What should be recorded before changing a lab network setting?
options: The symptom and current relevant configuration
mcqs.explanation: Before/after evidence makes troubleshooting assessable.

mcqs.question: Does a static-address fault necessarily disappear after DHCP renew?
options: Yes, every static setting is always replaced correctly
Only if the monitor is larger
Only if the computer name is shorter
mcqs.explanation: Diagnose the actual configuration method and fault.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: What is a useful first Packet Tracer LAN exercise?
options: Two PCs, a switch, compatible unique addresses and a peer test
Twenty unaddressed hosts with random cables and no plan
Deleting every host after placing it
mcqs.explanation: A small checked baseline makes later changes easier to diagnose.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: What should a two-group hub exercise account for?
options: Enough host ports and uplinks on the chosen models
No need for any address table
A claim that one eight-port hub has unlimited ports
mcqs.explanation: Actual port capacity constrains the topology.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: Does a layer-2 switch by itself route every pair of different IP subnets?
options: Yes, any management address creates all routes
Yes, every switch port is automatically a router
No, because switches cannot forward frames
mcqs.explanation: Inter-subnet forwarding requires appropriate layer-3 routing.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: What does a switch management IP primarily support?
options: Replacing host IP addresses on every data port
Making all connected hosts share the same IP
Changing a copper cable into fibre
mcqs.explanation: Management addressing is distinct from ordinary layer-2 frame forwarding.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: Which gateway suits PC-B 192.168.20.10/24 in the given routed lab?
mcqs.explanation: The gateway must be the reachable local router interface.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: What should be tested before a remote-subnet ping?
options: Local adapter/link settings and the local gateway
mcqs.explanation: Layered tests help locate the fault.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: What does a successful simulation not prove?
options: The saved lab file can be inspected
The specified virtual hosts exist in the lab
The real cable meets physical performance specifications
mcqs.explanation: Simulation does not replace physical certification.

mcqs.topic: 8.6 Packet Tracer networks, management and routing
mcqs.question: What should accompany a saved .pkt file?
options: Only a claim that nothing can fail
An address/port plan and expected-versus-observed evidence
mcqs.explanation: The lab should be reproducible and assessable.
